# Components

Which components the system carries: its inventory, picked from the catalogue.

## The five answers

| Question | Answer | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which component families does it need? | Actions, forms, feedback, overlays, layout and navigation | Forms, steps and feedback are all a public service needs. |
| How far does the inventory reach? | Only what today's screens use | Only the parts in use, each tested with assistive technology. |
| How does a component earn its place? | It works for everyone, with any device and assistive technology | A component joins only when it works with any device and assistive technology. |
| When does a component get another look? | Only when the meaning changes | One clear way to do each thing. |
| Where do components do the most work? | Forms and steps | Components do their work in forms and steps. |

## When to use what

| Situation | Use | Not | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| No component in the inventory fits | a native HTML element with a label and a hint | a custom widget that needs hover, drag or precise pointing | Native elements work with every assistive technology without extra work. |
